# javaw (Go)

Generates a small POSIX `sh` launcher script for a Java source file or jar. The
generated wrapper is the product; `javaw` never builds or launches anything.

## Build and run

```sh
go build -o javaw .
./javaw examples/HelloWorld.java            # writes ./run-hello-world
cp examples/HelloWorld.java . && ./run-hello-world Ada
./javaw --jar --min-java 17 --jvm-opts "-Xmx512m" -o bin/ tool.jar   # writes bin/run-tool
./javaw --help
```

Example output for `javaw --min-java 11 HelloWorld.java`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by: javaw --min-java 11 HelloWorld.java
self=$0
while [ -L "$self" ]; do
  link=$(readlink -- "$self")
  case $link in
    /*) self=$link ;;
    *) self=$(dirname -- "$self")/$link ;;
  esac
done
dir=$(CDPATH= cd -P -- "$(dirname -- "$self")" && pwd -P) || exit 1
v=$(java -version 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^[A-Za-z]* version "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
case $v in 1.*) n=${v#1.} ;; *) n=$v ;; esac
n=${n%%[!0-9]*}
if [ -z "$n" ] || [ "$n" -lt 11 ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "${0##*/}: requires Java 11 or newer (found: ${v:-none})" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exec java "$dir/HelloWorld.java" "$@"
```

Notes:
- The wrapper expects the program file (base name of the input) next to the wrapper's real file.
- `--jvm-opts` is inserted verbatim, so the shell splits it into separate options.
- Inputs that start with `-` go after `--`, e.g. `javaw -- -odd.java`.

## Tests and verification

```sh
go test ./...   # unit tests, plus real-java runs (skipped if java is missing)
./verify.sh     # demo: different dir, symlink, symlink chain, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, CDPATH
```

`go test` also runs every `--min-java` case (`1.8.0_x`, `28-ea`, a
`JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` notice, unparseable output, missing java) against fake JDKs
under both `/bin/sh` and `dash` (when installed), and covers a path starting with `-`.
